answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% cut, the incumbent has refused to reopen price, and the low-cost vendor's quote already hits the mandate on price alone (c2 confirms onboarding was fast and invoicing stayed accurate). c6 confirms multi-year terms with the incumbent previously cut unit cost, but that lever is closed because the incumbent refuses to reopen. With one sourcing decision available and the primary contract expiring in 14 days (no auto-renew), switching to the low-cost vendor is the only path that simultaneously meets the cost mandate and avoids a lapse in supply. Because the line is running at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, I will use a small, guarded first production run to verify the low-cost vendor's quality and on-time delivery in our actual operating conditions before scaling. This preserves delivery risk control while capturing the cost reduction c2's track record suggests is real.
